svg.title: Two assemblies of a small CP/M program and the PRL bitmap made from them
svg.desc: A seventeen-byte program assembled at 0000h and 0100h. Bytes 2 and 5, the high bytes of the addresses of MSG and PRINT, differ by one and are marked in the bitmap. Loaded at 8000h those two bytes become 80h while JP 0000h and JP BDOS are unchanged.
svg.text: Finding the addresses in a page-relocatable program
Assemble twice, mark the bytes that differ, then relocate by whole pages when loading
17 bytes of code give 3 bitmap bytes, 24 00 00h, bit 7 first. The last byte is padded with zeros.
loading at page 80h adds 7Fh to each marked byte
JP 0000h and JP BDOS keep their fixed addresses because they are the same in both assemblies.
Only the high bytes of addresses inside the program change, so one bit per byte is enough.
